careTips: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil is dry. Bright indirect light brings out the silver markings. Average humidity is fine but higher humidity encouraged for larger leaves. Let dry out slightly between waterings. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Also known as: Spiderwort. Fast-growing trailing plants in the Commelinaceae family with colorful striped or solid leaves.
commonExamples: Tradescantia zebrina (Wandering dude, Inch plant), T. pallida (Purple heart), T. fluminensis (Small-leaf spiderwort), T. spathacea (Moses-in-the-cradle)
careTips: Keep soil lightly moist, allow to dry slightly between waterings. Very fast-growing - may need frequent pruning. Bright indirect light maintains vibrant colors; low light causes leggy growth. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Pinch tips to encourage bushiness. Repot every 1-2 years. Perfect for hanging baskets. Easy to propagate from cuttings. Mildly toxic to pets -- causes mouth and skin irritation.

description: Trailing plant with thick, striped leaves in pink, green, and cream; compact, upright-then-cascading habit.
commonExamples: Tradescantia 'Nanouk'
careTips: Keep soil lightly moist. Bright indirect light maintains pink stripes. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Fast-growing. Mildly toxic to pets -- causes mouth and skin irritation. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Trim trailing stems to desired length. Prune leggy growth to encourage branching. Pinch growing tips for bushier growth.

description: Trailing plant with vivid purple foliage and small pink flowers; can be grown indoors or outdoors.
commonExamples: Tradescantia pallida (Purple heart)
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect to direct light enhances purple color. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Mildly toxic to pets -- causes mouth and skin irritation. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Houseplants with trailing or climbing growth habits, popular for hanging baskets and shelves. Many are fast-growing and easy to propagate.
commonExamples: Epipremnum aureum (Pothos), Hedera helix (English ivy), Tradescantia (Spiderwort), Hoya (Wax plant), Ceropegia woodii (String of hearts)
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Most are forgiving of occasional missed waterings. Bright indirect to medium light preferred — most tolerate lower light but may lose variegation. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine for most species. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength. Prune to control length and encourage bushier growth — cuttings root easily in water. Provide support (moss pole, trellis) for climbing species. Research specific species for exact requirements.

description: Tall fig tree with leathery, variegated leaves in shades of green and yellow. Also called council tree. Easier to care for than fiddle leaf fig.
commonExamples: Ficus altissima (Council tree), F. altissima 'Yellow Gem' (variegated cultivar)
careTips: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil is dry. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Average humidity is fine. Avoid moving frequently — can drop leaves from environmental changes. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: The more forgiving cousin of the Fiddle Leaf Fig, with velvety, oval leaves and pale trunk, increasingly popular as a statement houseplant.
commonExamples: Ficus benghalensis (Ficus Audrey, Banyan fig—indoor cultivar)
careTips: Water when top 2-5 cm of soil is dry; more forgiving than Fiddle Leaf Fig but still dislikes soggy soil. Bright indirect light preferred—tolerates some direct morning sun. Medium humidity fine. Well-draining potting mix. Fertilize monthly spring through fall at half strength. Wipe velvety leaves with damp cloth to remove dust. Less prone to leaf drop than Fiddle Leaf Fig but still dislikes being moved. Toxic to pets (milky latex sap). Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Ficus with glossy oval leaves, popular for bonsai; can develop aerial roots.
commonExamples: Ficus microcarpa (Chinese banyan, Ginseng ficus, Banyan fig), F. microcarpa 'Green Island'
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light. Often grown as bonsai. Avoid moving once established. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Also known as: FLF. Popular but finicky ficus with large violin-shaped leaves, requires consistent care and stable environment.
commonExamples: Ficus lyrata (Fiddle-leaf fig, FLF), F. lyrata 'Bambino' (compact variety), F. lyrata variegated (rare)
careTips: Water when top 2-3 inches of soil is dry. Very sensitive to overwatering and location changes - may drop leaves. Avoid drafts and sudden temperature changes. Bright indirect light essential - rotate regularly for even growth. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Wipe large leaves monthly. Repot every 2-3 years. Popular but finicky - requires consistent care and stable environment. Toxic to pets. Remove old, yellowing, or diseased leaves promptly.

description: Popular ficus with large, glossy dark green or burgundy leaves, can grow into a tree.
commonExamples: Ficus elastica (Rubber plant, Rubber tree), F. elastica 'Burgundy'
careTips: Water when top 2-3 inches of soil is dry. Avoid overwatering which causes root rot. Sensitive to location changes - may drop leaves when moved. Bright indirect light preferred; some direct morning sun is fine. Medium to high humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Wipe large glossy leaves monthly. Prune to control height. Repot every 2-3 years. Can grow into a tree. Toxic to pets.

description: Ficus elastica cultivar with dark burgundy, nearly black leaves; bold statement plant.
commonExamples: Ficus elastica 'Burgundy'
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; tolerates low light. Medium humidity (40-50%). Wipe leaves to remove dust. Toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

description: Striking Ficus elastica cultivar with tricolored leaves in deep green, cream, and vivid ruby-pink, especially vibrant on new growth.
commonExamples: Ficus elastica 'Ruby' (Ruby rubber plant, Pink rubber tree)
careTips: Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil feel dry; avoid overwatering which causes leaf drop. Bright indirect light is crucial to maintain the pink and cream variegation — low light causes reversion to green. Wipe the large, glossy leaves monthly with a damp cloth to keep them dust-free. Average room humidity is adequate. Fertilize monthly during spring and summer with balanced liquid fertilizer at half strength. Prune to control height and encourage branching. Mildly toxic — the milky sap can irritate skin and is harmful to pets if ingested.

description: Fast-growing grasses in the Poaceae family, can be clumping or running types, popular for screening and containers.
commonExamples: Bambusa (Clumping bamboo), Phyllostachys (Running bamboo), Fargesia (Cold-hardy clumping bamboo), indoor varieties like Dracaena sanderiana (Lucky bamboo)
careTips: Keep soil consistently moist (2-3 times per week). Running types spread aggressively - contain with barriers or plant in containers. Clumping types are more manageable. Full sun to partial shade depending on species. Fertilize monthly during growing season with high-nitrogen fertilizer. Prune to control height and remove old canes. Container-grown bamboo needs regular repotting. Research clumping vs running types before planting. Some species are invasive - check local regulations. Indoor lucky bamboo grows in water or soil.

description: Also known as: Crane flower. Large tropical plants in the Strelitziaceae family with distinctive bird-like flowers and banana-like leaves.
commonExamples: Strelitzia reginae (Bird of paradise, Crane flower), S. nicolai (Giant white bird of paradise, Wild banana)
careTips: Water when top 2 inches of soil is dry. Keep consistently moist in growing season, reduce in winter. Bright indirect to direct light preferred - needs lots of light to flower. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Wipe large leaves monthly. Repot every 2-3 years. Distinctive bird-like flowers. Can grow quite large - provide adequate space. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Also known as: Giant bird of paradise. Large tropical plant with banana-like leaves and striking white and blue crane-shaped flowers. Grows to 6m outdoors; popular as dramatic indoor foliage plant.
commonExamples: Strelitzia nicolai (White bird of paradise, Giant bird of paradise)
careTips: Water when top 5cm of soil is dry; reduce in winter. Bright indirect to direct light — more light encourages flowering. Medium humidity sufficient but appreciates higher. Large plant that needs space; repot every 2-3 years. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer. Leaves may split naturally with age. Prune dead leaves at base. Mildly toxic to pets.

description: Miniature trees created through cultivation techniques - care varies by species, this is a general guide.
commonExamples: Juniperus (Juniper), Ficus, Acer (Maple), Pinus (Pine)
careTips: Water when soil surface is dry - check daily as small pots dry quickly. Avoid both over and under-watering. Adjust based on species needs - research your specific tree type. Bright indirect to direct light depending on species. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with bonsai fertilizer. Prune regularly to maintain shape. Repot every 2-3 years with bonsai soil mix. Requires patience and consistent care. Each species has specific requirements.
origin: East Asia (art form originating in China, refined in Japan)

description: Also known as: Painted nettle. Colorful foliage plants in the Lamiaceae family with vibrant leaves in various patterns and colors, pinch flowers to maintain foliage.
commonExamples: Coleus scutellarioides (syn. Plectranthus scutellarioides, Solenostemon scutellarioides) (Coleus, Painted nettle), various hybrid cultivars
careTips: Keep soil evenly moist, avoid letting dry out. Bright indirect light maintains vibrant colors; direct sun may fade colors. High humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize every 2 weeks spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Pinch flower spikes to redirect energy into leaf growth and maintain the best foliage color, though flowering does not kill the plant. Pinch tips regularly to maintain bushy growth. Repot annually. Easy to propagate from cuttings. Annual in most climates. Mildly toxic to pets if ingested.

description: Tropical foliage plant with sword-shaped leaves in vibrant reds, pinks, purples, and greens. The Hawaiian ti plant holds deep cultural significance in Polynesian traditions.
commonExamples: Cordyline fruticosa (Ti plant, Good luck plant), C. australis (Cabbage tree, New Zealand cabbage palm), C. terminalis (syn. C. fruticosa)
careTips: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil are dry; keep evenly moist but not soggy. Bright indirect light for best color; tolerates lower light but colors fade. Medium humidity (50%+). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer. Prune leggy stems by cutting back — new growth sprouts from below the cut. Brown leaf tips indicate low humidity or fluoride sensitivity — use filtered water. Hawaiian ti leaves are used for wrapping food and making hula skirts. Toxic to cats and dogs — causes vomiting and depression.

description: World's largest unbranched flower structure, producing a massive spathe that smells of rotting flesh when blooming. Blooms are rare, occurring every 7-10 years.
commonExamples: Amorphophallus titanum (Titan arum, Corpse flower). Distinct from Rafflesia, which is the world's largest individual flower
careTips: Keep soil consistently moist but well-drained during active growth. Bright indirect light. Very high humidity (70-80%) required. Goes completely dormant after flowering — reduce water drastically. Requires large pot (60+ cm) for mature corm. Fertilize monthly during growing season with balanced fertilizer. Grows from a massive underground corm. Prefers acidic soil. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or yellowing foliage. Prune to maintain desired shape.

description: Also known as: Garden croton. Colorful tropical foliage plants in the Euphorbiaceae family with vibrant leaves in red, orange, yellow, and green, sensitive to changes.
commonExamples: Codiaeum variegatum (Croton, Garden croton), C. variegatum 'Petra', C. variegatum 'Mammy'
careTips: Keep soil evenly moist, avoid letting dry out. High humidity (60%+) preferred - use humidifier. Bright indirect to direct light essential to maintain vibrant colors. Sensitive to changes - avoid moving once established. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. May drop leaves if stressed (drafts, temperature changes, low humidity). Repot every 1-2 years. Wipe leaves monthly. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Croton cultivar with twisted, spiral leaves in red, orange, yellow, and green.
commonExamples: Codiaeum variegatum 'Mammy'
careTips: Keep soil evenly moist, avoid letting dry out. Bright indirect to direct light essential for vibrant colors. High humidity (60%+) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Sensitive to drafts and changes. Toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Ancient palm-like plants in the Cycadaceae family, slow-growing with stiff fronds, many are endangered in the wild.
commonExamples: Cycas revoluta (Sago palm, King sago), Zamia (Coontie, Cardboard palm), Dioon (Dioon cycad), Macrozamia
careTips: Water when top 2-3 inches of soil is dry. Allow to dry slightly between waterings - avoid overwatering which causes root rot. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Low to medium humidity is fine. Fertilize 2-3 times per year during growing season with palm fertilizer. Very slow-growing - repot every 3-5 years. Remove dead fronds at base. Toxic to pets if ingested. Ancient plants that have existed for millions of years. Research specific species for exact requirements. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

description: Bold tropical foliage plant with large, deeply lobed palmately compound leaves.
commonExamples: Fatsia japonica (Japanese aralia, Paper plant), F. japonica 'Spider Web'
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light; tolerates lower light. High humidity preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Can grow large; prune to control size. Toxic to pets.

description: Striking tropical plant with deeply textured, dark purple-black suckered leaves that shimmer in the light. A trending collector plant.
commonExamples: Geogenanthus ciliatus (Geo plant, Seersucker plant)
careTips: Keep soil consistently moist — sensitive to drought; leaf edges crisp quickly if too dry. Medium indirect light; avoid direct sun. High humidity (60%+) critical — brown leaf edges indicate low humidity. Well-draining, moisture-retentive mix. Fertilize monthly spring through fall at quarter strength. Slow grower. Sensitive to cold — keep above 18°C. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or yellowing foliage. Prune to maintain desired shape.

description: Tropical rhizomatous plants with spectacular waxy bracts in red, orange, yellow, and pink. Related to banana and bird of paradise.
commonExamples: Heliconia rostrata (Hanging lobster claw), H. psittacorum (Parrot's beak), H. bihai (Red palulu), H. caribaea (Caribbean heliconia)
careTips: Water frequently — heliconias are heavy drinkers that need consistently moist soil. Bright indirect light indoors; filtered sun outdoors. Rich, acidic, well-drained soil with high organic matter. Very high humidity (70%+) essential — mist daily or use a humidifier. Fertilize every 2 weeks during growing season with balanced fertilizer. Protect from temperatures below 15°C. Remove dead or damaged leaves at the base. Excellent cut flowers that last 1-2 weeks. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Bright golden conifer with lemony scent, popular as indoor or patio plant, requires good air circulation.
commonExamples: Cupressus macrocarpa 'Goldcrest' (Lemon cypress, Goldcrest cypress, Monterey cypress 'Goldcrest')
careTips: Keep soil moist but not waterlogged. Excellent drainage essential. Allow top inch to dry slightly between waterings. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Good air circulation essential - avoid stagnant air. Medium humidity (40-50%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Prune to maintain shape. Repot every 2-3 years. Bright golden color with lemony scent. Popular as indoor or patio plant.

description: Also known as: Chinese water bamboo. Dracaena species often grown in water or soil, popular for feng shui, not a true bamboo.
commonExamples: Dracaena sanderiana (Lucky bamboo, Chinese water bamboo, Ribbon plant)
careTips: In water: Change water weekly, keep water level consistent. In soil: Water when top inch is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Medium humidity is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength (if in soil) or add to water monthly. Can be grown in water indefinitely or in soil. Popular for feng shui arrangements. Not a true bamboo. Toxic to pets. Repot every 2-3 years if in soil. Remove yellowing or damaged leaves promptly.

description: Tropical tree with palmate leaves, often sold with braided trunk; symbol of prosperity and good luck.
commonExamples: Pachira aquatica (Money tree, Guiana chestnut, Malabar chestnut)
careTips: Water when top 2 inches of soil is dry. Avoid overwatering which causes root rot—very sensitive to soggy soil. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium to high humidity (50-60%) preferred. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Often sold with braided trunk—don't untie. Repot every 2-3 years. Remove yellowing leaves. Non-toxic to pets. Remove yellowing or dead leaves promptly.

description: Also known as: Mosaic plant. Colorful foliage plants in the Acanthaceae family with distinctive veining in various colors, will wilt dramatically when thirsty.
commonExamples: Fittonia albivenis, F. verschaffeltii (Nerve plant, Mosaic plant), F. 'Pink Angel', F. 'Red Anne'
careTips: Keep soil evenly moist, never let dry. High humidity (70%+) essential - use humidifier or terrarium. Will wilt dramatically when thirsty but recovers quickly when watered. Bright indirect light preferred; direct sun burns leaves. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Pinch tips to encourage bushiness. Repot every 1-2 years. Perfect for terrariums. Distinctive veining in various colors.

description: Also known as: Star pine. Indoor conifer native to Norfolk Island, popular as holiday plant, not a true pine but resembles one, sensitive to dry air. Requires consistent moisture.
commonExamples: Araucaria heterophylla (Norfolk Island pine, Star pine)
careTips: Keep soil evenly moist, avoid drying out completely. High humidity (50-60%) preferred - mist regularly in dry conditions or use humidifier. Bright indirect light preferred; some direct morning sun is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Sensitive to dry air - brown needles indicate low humidity. Repot every 2-3 years. Popular as holiday plant. Not a true pine despite the name. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Plants in the Oxalidaceae family with clover-like leaves that fold at night, some species go dormant seasonally.
commonExamples: Oxalis triangularis (Purple shamrock, False shamrock), O. regnellii (Green shamrock, Lucky clover)
careTips: Keep soil moist during active growth. Reduce significantly or stop watering during dormancy when leaves die back - this is normal. Bright indirect to direct light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly during active growth with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Clover-like leaves fold at night. Some species go dormant seasonally - don't discard, it will regrow. Repot every 2-3 years. Toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Also known as: False shamrock. Clover-like plant with purple triangular leaves that fold at night; produces small pink or white flowers.
commonExamples: Oxalis triangularis (Purple shamrock, False shamrock)
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; some direct morning sun enhances purple. Medium humidity (40-50%). Goes dormant periodically—reduce watering when leaves die back. Fertilize monthly during active growth. Toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Compact tropical foliage plants in the Piperaceae family with thick, succulent-like leaves.
commonExamples: Peperomia obtusifolia (Baby rubber plant), P. caperata (Ripple peperomia), P. argyreia (Watermelon peperomia), P. 'Hope', P. 'Rosso'
careTips: Water when top 2 inches of soil is dry. More drought tolerant than many tropical plants due to succulent-like leaves. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Compact growth habit. Repot every 2-3 years. Easy-care houseplants. Thick, succulent-like leaves store water. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Compact peperomia with deeply ridged, heart-shaped leaves in red, green, or silver.
commonExamples: Peperomia caperata (Emerald ripple)
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Susceptible to overwatering. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Peperomia with thick, glossy oval leaves; upright or trailing, not a true rubber plant.
commonExamples: Peperomia obtusifolia (Baby rubber plant)
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Tolerates low light. Non-toxic to pets. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Compact peperomia with deeply ridged, dark green leaves and striking red undersides. Semi-succulent with low water needs. Excellent desk plant.
commonExamples: Peperomia caperata 'Rosso' (Emerald ripple pepper, Red ripple peperomia)
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry; semi-succulent so tolerates slight drought. Bright indirect light enhances red coloring. Average humidity is fine. Compact grower rarely needing repotting. Fertilize lightly spring through summer. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Compact peperomia with silver-striped leaves resembling watermelon rind.
commonExamples: Peperomia argyreia (Watermelon peperomia, syn. P. sandersii)
careTips: Water when top 2 inches of soil is dry. Allow to dry between waterings. Bright indirect light maintains silver stripes. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Silver-striped leaves resembling watermelon rind. Compact growth habit. Repot every 2-3 years. Easy-care houseplant. Non-toxic to pets. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Compact tropical foliage plants in the Urticaceae family with round or textured leaves.
commonExamples: Pilea peperomioides (Chinese money plant, Pancake plant, UFO plant), P. cadierei (Aluminum plant), P. involucrata (Friendship plant)
careTips: Water when top 2 inches of soil is dry. Allow to dry between waterings. Avoid overwatering. Bright indirect light preferred. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Compact growth habit. Round or textured leaves. Repot every 1-2 years. Easy to propagate from offsets or cuttings. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly., if planted in water, need to clean rotted root

description: Also known as: UFO plant. Popular Pilea with round, coin-like leaves on upright stems.
commonExamples: Pilea peperomioides (Chinese money plant, Pancake plant, UFO plant)
careTips: Water when top 2 inches of soil is dry. Allow to dry between waterings. Bright indirect light preferred; rotate regularly for even growth. Medium humidity (40-50%) is fine. Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Produces offsets (pups) that can be separated and repotted. Repot every 1-2 years. Round, coin-like leaves on upright stems. Popular and easy-care. Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly., if planted in water, need to clean rotted root

description: Compact pilea with quilted, bronze-veined leaves; easy to propagate and share—hence the name.
commonExamples: Pilea involucrata (Friendship plant)
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light preferred; avoid direct sun. Medium humidity (40-50%). Fertilize monthly spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Easy to propagate from cuttings. Repot every 1-2 years when roots fill container. Resistant to pruning, Remove dead or damaged foliage promptly.

description: Also known as: Kusamaki. Conifer-like evergreen with narrow leaves, popular for bonsai and topiary.
commonExamples: Podocarpus macrophyllus (Buddhist pine, Kusamaki, Yew pine), P. henkelii
careTips: Water when top inch of soil is dry. Bright indirect light. Tolerates lower light. Fertilize monthly spring through fall. Prune to maintain shape. Good for bonsai. Toxic to pets.

description: Colorful foliage plants in the Acanthaceae family with spotted leaves in pink, red, or white, pinch to maintain bushy growth.
commonExamples: Hypoestes phyllostachya (Polka dot plant, Freckle face), various color cultivars
careTips: Keep soil evenly moist, avoid letting dry out. High humidity (60%+) preferred - use humidifier or pebble tray. Bright indirect light maintains vibrant colors. Fertilize every 2 weeks spring through fall with balanced fertilizer at half strength. Pinch tips regularly to encourage branching and maintain bushy growth. Pinch flowers immediately to prolong plant life. Repot annually. Annual in most climates. Easy to propagate from cuttings.

description: World's largest individual flower, up to 1m diameter and weighing 11kg. A parasitic plant with no stems, leaves, or roots — it lives entirely within a host vine and only emerges to bloom.
commonExamples: Rafflesia arnoldii (Corpse lily), R. keithii, R. tuan-mudae
careTips: Cannot be cultivated outside its native Southeast Asian rainforest habitat. Parasitizes Tetrastigma vines. Requires specific tropical conditions: 70-90% humidity, 22-32°C, deep shade. Blooms last only 5-7 days and smell of rotting flesh to attract pollinating flies. Several species critically endangered. Botanical gardens worldwide have attempted cultivation with extremely limited success. Non-toxic. Remove dead or yellowing foliage. Prune to maintain desired shape.

description: One of the most unusual plants on Earth — a living fossil from the Namib Desert. Each plant produces only two leaves in its entire lifetime, which grow continuously and split into straps. Can live over 1,000 years.
commonExamples: Welwitschia mirabilis (Welwitschia, Tree tumbo, Tweeblaarkanniedood)
careTips: Extremely drought tolerant but benefits from occasional deep watering. Full sun. Excellent drainage is critical — grows naturally in desert sand and gravel. Very slow growing. Nearly impossible to transplant due to a deep taproot. Non-toxic. Remove dead or yellowing foliage. Prune to maintain desired shape.
